{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — IBM Facilities/Hosted Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of the Agreement (Base Terms), including § 3.1 Term
**Status of findings:** Verified findings as supplied; verification step recorded as skipped for each item.

---

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against our playbook and identified 19 findings: three critical deviations, six high-severity items (four deviations, two compliant), eight medium items (four deviations, one missing, three compliant), and one low-severity gap.

The commercial shape of the deal is workable, but the risk allocation is materially one-sided in IBM's favour in three respects. First, on **liability** (§ 9.1), the cap floor is $100,000 measured on charges "paid" only, there are no carve-outs for confidentiality, data protection, gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and § 9.1(c)(2) excludes IBM's liability entirely for loss of or damage to our records and data — the core risk in a hosting arrangement. Second, on **IP** (§ 5.4 / Section 7), the default is IBM-owned Type II Materials with a narrow internal-use licence back to us, while for Materials we do own IBM receives an irrevocable, worldwide licence to distribute externally; there is no express statement that we retain ownership of Content or Customer Components. Third, on **indemnities** (§ 8.1–8.2), IBM gives an IP infringement indemnity only, while our indemnity at 8.2(3) extends to any Services Recipient claim relating directly or indirectly to IBM's own Services — a one-way indemnity for the Vendor's services.

On **exit**, our termination for convenience right (§ 3.4) is conditioned on uncapped, undefined early termination charges, with no refund of prepaid Charges anywhere in the Agreement, and § 3.5 contains no transition assistance, data return, export or deletion obligations. Renewal (§ 3.2) auto-renews for a term equal to the prior term (permitting automatic multi-year renewals) on 90 days' notice, with no cap on renewal Charges.

On the positive side, the Agreement imposes **no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum purchase commitment or employee non-solicitation** on us, and § 14.16 (Freedom of Action) affirmatively preserves our ability to source competing services. Governing law is New York, which is our preferred position; the only gap is the absence of a forum/venue provision.

---

## Findings table

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 8.1 Indemnification by IBM |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 5.4 Other Disclaimers |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Deviation | § 9.1 IBM's Limitation of Liability |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 14.10 Assignment |
| 5 | High | LD — Liquidated damages/penalties payable by Customer | Deviation | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience |
| 6 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 12.1 License |
| 7 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience |
| 8 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action |
| 9 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 11.3 Suspected Violations |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 14.3 Choice of Law |
| 12 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Deviation | § 3.2 Renewal |
| 13 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 5.1 IBM Representations and Warranties |
| 14 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 3.5 Effect of Termination |
| 15 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action |
| 16 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments/volume restrictions | Compliant | § 4.1 Charges |
| 17 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant | § 14.8 Personnel |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 14.12 Risk of Loss |

---

## Walk-away items

The following findings were assessed as at or approaching our playbook walk-away line. We should not sign without movement on these:

1. **One-way indemnity for IBM's own Services (§ 8.2(3)).** Our indemnity covers any Services Recipient claim relating directly or indirectly to IBM's Services, only partially offset by the carve-back in 8.2(c). We propose narrowing this to our breach of applicable law, leaving the Content/AUP and mechanics' lien prongs intact.
2. **Exclusion of IBM liability for loss of or damage to our records and data (§ 9.1(c)(2)).** In a hosting deal this excludes the central risk, and § 6 reinforces it by giving §§ 5, 9 and 10 precedence over the confidentiality agreement. We propose deleting the exclusion, raising the mutual cap floor to $1,000,000 on fees paid or payable, and adding a mutual uncapped carve-out sentence.
3. **At-will revocable licence (§ 12.1).** The Base Components licence is expressly "revocable" with no breach or cure predicate, and § 14.17 confirms no rights beyond those expressly granted. We propose limiting revocation to uncured material breach and extending the grant to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf.
4. **Uncapped early termination charges (§ 3.4(b), with § 10).** The charges are undefined in the Agreement and cross-referenced to attachments not before us, potentially approaching remaining contract value. Fallback: cap at three months' recurring Charges as the sole liquidated amount on termination.
5. **Automatic multi-year renewal (§ 3.2).** Renewal for a term equal in duration to the prior term, with no cap on renewal Charges. We propose fixing renewals at 12 months with 30 days' notice, a 60-day reminder and a CPI/3% uplift cap.
6. **Unlimited, unannounced investigation right (§ 11.3).** No frequency, notice, business-hours, confidentiality or cost limits, and no exclusion of access to our systems. Fallback: 15 days' notice / 10% threshold formulation.
7. **"AS IS" disclaimer swallowing the express warranty (§ 5.4(c) with § 5.1).** IBM warrants only reasonable care and skill, with no conformance warranty, warranty period or remedy for Materials.

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline.** The proposed changes are drafted for §§ 3.2, 3.4, 3.5, 5.1, 5.4(c), 8.1, 8.2(3), 9.1, 11.3, 12.1, 14.3, 14.10 and a new § 14.12A (insurance), plus the Section 7 Materials ownership flip to Type I with a broadened Type II licence-back and an express Customer Data/Content ownership and no-joint-ownership statement.
2. **Prioritise negotiation** in the order set out above: liability and data-loss exclusion, IP ownership, indemnity symmetry, then exit economics (early termination charges, prepaid refund, transition assistance).
3. **Obtain the missing attachments.** Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments govern Charges and early termination charges but are not part of this document. We should confirm at Order Form stage that any early termination charge is a true-up for services actually ordered rather than a penalty or disguised minimum commitment (per the MINCOMMIT watch item).
4. **Confirm insurance appetite** with IBM, offering the fallback of E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M against our opening position of CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M and statutory workers' compensation, with certificates on request.
5. **Complete verification.** Verification was skipped for all findings; we should re-run confirmation of section references against the executed form before the redline is exchanged.
6. **Preserve the compliant positions.** No changes are needed to §§ 14.16, 14.8, 14.11 or 4.1, and we should resist any counter-proposal that introduces exclusivity, MFN, minimum volume or non-solicit obligations on us."}
